notes: Web search ran out for the whole session after eleven searches in this part (the tool reported 200 of 200 used), so the rest was done by reading known pages directly with the kit's own User-Agent: the campaign sites the candidates filed, governments' own pages, the Minnesota DFL's endorsed list, the Minnesota Legislative Manual 2025-2026, the University of Minnesota's election archive and KAXE's election guides. A campaign site nobody filed could not be looked for, so a missing website here is not proof that none exists.

No party's own page naming Sue Ek or George Gilmour as endorsed was found: mngop.com's '2026 Republican Nominees' page gave this reader no text with either name, and no local Republican unit's address was known. KNSI reported a Republican endorsement of Sue Ek on February 21, 2026; a news report is not a party's own page, so nothing is recorded.
Out of reach and not worked around: www.co.houston.mn.us refused the secure connection (Dean Mierau); www.perham.k12.mn.us did not answer (Danielle Collins); mncourts.gov refuses scripts.

Checked and nothing found on the government's own page (not on the present board or council, or the page names nobody): Dean Mierau (the Legislative Manual lists Eric Johnson in Houston County District 2), Tina King (Steven J. Rohlfing holds Le Sueur District 5), Rebecca Trapp (the Manual lists Maggie Kluver as Big Stone County Attorney; the county's Attorney pages name no one), Brad Johnson (Austin), Jodi Justice (North St. Paul), Benjamin Sykora (Victoria), Ethan Becker (Owatonna), Katie Large (Detroit Lakes), Christopher Reilly (Grand Rapids), Christine Estee (South St. Paul).
No birth year is recorded for anyone. KAXE's guides give an 'Age on Election Day' (Tad A. Erickson 41, Christopher Reilly 44), which fits two calendar years, so it is left out.
